annotation.kind: source selection, equation-(1) radix model, and equation-(8) exact-subtraction implication

assumptions: The format has an arbitrary integer radix beta >= 2, positive precision p, and an inclusive finite exponent interval [emin, emax] as in equation (1).
The finite system is equation (1) written in its equivalent canonical split into zero, normalized values, and values at the lower-exponent subnormal lattice.
The exponents ex and ey are normalized exponents; subtracting p from either gives an equation-(1) exponent for the corresponding input.
The operands x and y have normalized representations in the same format.
The exact difference satisfies the magnitude premise of equation (8), reindexed as |x-y| <= beta^min(ex,ey).
The strict upper-exponent premise expresses the paper's absence-of-overflow qualification, including the equality endpoint of the magnitude bound.
The computed subtraction is faithfully rounded, with no fixed tie rule.
The real-valued model has no infinities, NaNs, exception flags, or signed-zero distinction.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P12 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P12 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p12_t1_exact_subtraction (fmt : P12RadixFormat) (x y rounded : Real) (ex ey : Int) (hx : P12NormalizedExponentRepresentation fmt x ex) (hy : P12NormalizedExponentRepresentation fmt y ey) (hmag : abs (x-y) <= fmt.betaR ^ min ex ey) (hnoOverflow : min ex ey < fmt.normalEmax) (hround : p12FaithfulInFormat fmt (x-y) rounded) : p12FiniteSystem fmt (x-y) and rounded=x-y
formal_statement.plain_language: Equation (8): a nonoverflowing difference that remains within one radix binade of the operands' common lattice is representable, so faithful subtraction returns the exact difference.

informal_proof: Write both operands on the lower of their two radix lattices. The magnitude bound limits the signed integer coefficient of their difference to p digits. Renormalize that coefficient, or place it on the lower-exponent lattice if it remains subnormal; the equality endpoint is a minimum-mantissa value at the next exponent and the overflow premise keeps that exponent in range. Since the exact difference belongs to F, faithful rounding must return it.
informal_statement: The exact-subtraction implication numbered (8) in the proof of Theorem 2, including its common-radix-lattice, magnitude, absence-of-overflow, representability, and faithful-rounding content.
